set.body:
Carry the recall-audio clock into the Sherlock recall-to-video report.

The Zenodo recall CSVs give a measured onset second for (most) words, and the runner discards
them after parsing: units are reported in film time only. The scientific deliverable is a
crosswalk between the recall-audio timeline and the film playback timeline, so each report row
should carry the unit's recall-audio timing next to its media coordinate.

Slice: a pure RecallTiming helper in the runner file computes each word's character span in
the transcript (words joined by single spaces - the exact text the segmenter ran on), then for
each recall unit takes the words overlapping its span and publishes onsetSeconds (first word
in the unit carrying a measured onset) and lastWordOnsetSeconds (last such word). No offset or
duration is fabricated: the CSVs measure onsets only, and the column names say which estimand
they carry. Units whose words all lack onsets publish empty cells, never zeros.

Report gains recallOnsetSeconds and recallLastWordOnsetSeconds columns.

Evidence: unit test deriving expected onsets independently from a synthetic CSV; scoped gate
on embed-bench.
set.title: Recall-audio timing columns in the Sherlock recall report
